case.case_id: S.C. (Special) No. 117/97 with S.C. Application No. 858/97
case.case_title: Dissanayake v. Premaratne, Inspector of Police, Nuwara-Eliya
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1998) 2 Sri L.R. 211

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained without being brought before a judge as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained at the Police Station for over 24 hours without being produced before a Magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended the detention was lawful and within 24 hours, and that the petitioner was released on Police bail without delay.
key_facts: Petitioner and his wife were detained at the Police Station from about 3 p.m. on 8.5.1997 until 5.30 p.m. on 9.5.1997.
Petitioner was not produced before a Magistrate during this detention period.
Petitioner was released on Police bail without a Magistrate's order.
Respondents claimed detention was lawful pending investigation.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that Article 13(2) requires that any person detained must be brought before a judge within a reasonable time and cannot be held without a legal order. Detention exceeding 24 hours without production before a Magistrate violates this provision.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found the petitioner was detained for more than 24 hours without being produced before a Magistrate and was released on Police bail without judicial authorization, breaching Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge within 24 hours is unlawful.
Release on Police bail without Magistrate's order does not satisfy Article 13(2).

outcome.holding: The Court held that the respondents violated the petitioner's fundamental rights under Article 13(2) by detaining him without producing him before a judge and without a legal order.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation and costs were awarded to the petitioner for the violation of Article 13(2).

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was crucial in establishing the unlawfulness of the petitioner's detention without judicial oversight, directly supporting the Court's relief for fundamental rights violations.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was detained at the Police Station for over 24 hours without being produced before a Magistrate and was released on Police bail without a Magistrate's order.
